summary: Namibia has no national school-device rule or social media age limit yet. A data protection bill and a cybercrime bill are still being finalized, and a ban on social media for under-15s is being debated.
school_devices: No national rule found. UNESCO reports no ban on mobile devices in classrooms, and the national ICT in education policy encourages technology use.
social_media_age: No national rule found. A ban on social media for under-15s was debated publicly in 2026, but nothing has been enacted.
child_data_law: No comprehensive data protection law in force. A Data Protection Bill, which would require parental consent before collecting children's data, was tabled in 2025; in January 2026 the ICT minister said it and a Cybercrime Bill were still being finalized.
worth_knowing: The ICT ministry launched a national portal for anonymously reporting child sexual abuse material, with the Internet Watch Foundation, UNICEF, and Lifeline/ChildLine Namibia, and urged parents to monitor the devices they give children.

summary: Senegal banned phones in all schools from the 2025-26 school year and relies on general data and cybercrime laws. No social media age limit was found.
school_devices: The Education Ministry banned mobile phones in public and private schools from the 2025-26 school year, with exceptions. The rule doesn't mention wearables.
social_media_age: No national rule found.
child_data_law: Data Protection Act (Law 2008-12) and Cybercrime Law (2008). Legal analysts note the data law has no child-specific protections.
worth_knowing: The school ban was framed around concentration and learning, with exceptions for medical needs and supervised learning.

summary: South Africa has strong child data protections and provincial school rules, but no national school ban or social media age limit.
school_devices: No national ban. Western Cape's 2025 guidelines let schools regulate phones and wearables, mostly limiting use to teacher-directed learning.
social_media_age: No national rule found.
child_data_law: Protection of Personal Information Act 2013 (POPIA) restricts processing children's data without a guardian's consent. The Cybercrimes Act 2020 covers online harms.
worth_knowing: Western Cape guidance names smartwatches as devices schools can ban during exams. A parent campaign is petitioning for phone-free schools nationwide.

summary: Nigeria requires parental consent for children's data, and is consulting on rules for under-16s online, but no school ban or social media age limit is in force.
school_devices: No national rule found.
social_media_age: No enacted age limit. In 2026 the government began consultations on age restrictions and verification and announced plans to regulate internet access for under-16s.
child_data_law: Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023, which requires parental consent and age verification for children's data. The Child Rights Act also applies.
worth_knowing: The consultations cover age verification and platform accountability, so rules may be coming.

summary: Kenya has strong child data rules and child online safety guidance for industry, but no nationwide school phone ban or social media age limit.
school_devices: No single national rule found, though phones are widely barred in schools in practice.
social_media_age: No national rule found. Data protection rules require age verification and parental consent for children's data.
child_data_law: Data Protection Act 2019 (section 33) and 2021 regulations require parental consent and put children's best interests first.
worth_knowing: 2025 industry guidelines tell telecom and mobile companies to build age verification and child safety by design.

summary: Since September 2026, Egypt bars social media accounts for under-13s and requires a locked Safe Mode for ages 13 and 14.
school_devices: No national rule in force. The Information Minister called for a school phone ban in February 2026 while Parliament discussed a draft.
social_media_age: Platforms may not create accounts for under-13s. Ages 13 to 14 get accounts only with age verification and a Safe Mode that can't be turned off.
child_data_law: Personal Data Protection Law No. 151 of 2020 requires a guardian's consent for children's data.
worth_knowing: Platforms must review existing minors' accounts, offer age-correction appeals, and comply within three months.

summary: China lets schools ban smart devices and requires real-identity checks and minor modes across online services.
school_devices: 2021 Ministry of Education rules let schools prohibit phones and other smart devices, with classroom use only for teaching. Smartwatches aren't named.
social_media_age: No single age limit. Minor modes are mandatory, and a September 2026 draft would push under-16s into minor mode on social apps.
child_data_law: Personal Information Protection Law 2021 and the Minor Online Protection Regulation 2023.
worth_knowing: Kids' watches here work like a social network, with likes and rankings on the leading brand.

summary: Singapore's schools ban smartphones and smartwatches outside lessons, and children's data is protected under general privacy law.
school_devices: From January 2026, secondary students may not use smartphones or smartwatches outside lessons, including recess. Primary rules began in January 2025.
social_media_age: No legal age limit. Parental consent is required for data collection under 13.
child_data_law: Personal Data Protection Act 2012, with 2024 guidelines for children's data.
worth_knowing: The Education Ministry included smartwatches specifically because they allow messaging and social media.

summary: South Korea put a classroom ban on phones and smart devices into law from March 2026.
school_devices: The amended Elementary and Secondary Education Act bars phones and smart devices during class from March 2026, and lets schools restrict them on campus.
social_media_age: No national rule found.
child_data_law: Personal Information Protection Act 2011.
worth_knowing: Exemptions cover disability, learning needs, and emergencies. Schools set the details.

summary: Japan leaves school phone rules to local authorities and requires filtering for young users.
school_devices: National guidance recommends not bringing phones to elementary and junior high schools. Details are local.
social_media_age: No national rule found.
child_data_law: Act on a Safe Internet Environment for Young People (2008), which requires filtering and parental controls. General data law also applies.
worth_knowing: Toyoake city's 2025 ordinance suggests two hours of leisure screen time a day, as guidance with no penalties.

summary: India has strong child data rules on paper but no national school ban or social media age limit.
school_devices: No national rule found.
social_media_age: No age limit. The data law treats under-18s as children and requires verifiable parental consent.
child_data_law: Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023, which bans tracking and targeted ads aimed at children.
worth_knowing: The government told Parliament it had not set a minimum social media age.

summary: Indonesia has age-graded rules for children's online platforms and limits gadgets during school lessons.
school_devices: A 2026 ministry circular restricts devices during lessons and lets schools adapt the rules. It is not a full ban.
social_media_age: Government Regulation 17/2025 requires age verification and parental consent, and limits under-13s to low-risk services built for children.
child_data_law: Government Regulation 17/2025 on child protection online.
worth_knowing: The rules use age bands (3 to 5, 6 to 9, 10 to 12, 13 to 15, 16 to 18) and require parental supervision tools.

summary: The Philippines has strong child privacy guidance, while school device and social media limits are still proposals.
school_devices: A Senate bill would ban devices, including smartwatches, during class from kindergarten through senior high. Not yet enacted.
social_media_age: No national rule found. Senate proposals include age verification and restrictions.
child_data_law: Data Privacy Act 2012, with 2024 guidance on age assurance and privacy by default for children.
worth_knowing: The privacy regulator warns that a child simply typing in an age isn't enough for risky services.

summary: Germany has no federal school ban, but states restrict devices, and watches with secret listen-in features are illegal.
school_devices: No national rule. Schleswig-Holstein's 2025 rules cover smartphones and smartwatches, with exceptions for teaching and emergencies.
social_media_age: Digital consent age under GDPR is 16.
child_data_law: EU GDPR plus German data law, and the Youth Protection Act for online media.
worth_knowing: Kids' watches with a hidden listen-in function have been banned since 2017. Stiftung Warentest rated Xplora and Garmin Bounce best.

summary: Norway recommends phone-free schools and plans a higher social media age limit, not yet in force.
school_devices: A national recommendation removes phones from classrooms and strongly limits private phones and smartwatches. Schools adopt it locally.
social_media_age: The government proposed an age limit allowing social media from the year a child turns 16, and raising digital consent age to 15.
child_data_law: Personal Data Act 2018 with GDPR.
worth_knowing: A government white paper found almost a third of children aged 5 to 8 use a smartwatch.

summary: UK schools are expected to be phone-free all day, online services have child safety duties, and an under-16 social media ban is planned.
school_devices: Statutory guidance expects schools to ban phones and similar smart devices all day, which generally includes smartwatches that can message or record.
social_media_age: No age limit yet. The government announced a planned under-16 ban, expected no earlier than spring 2027.
child_data_law: Online Safety Act 2023, UK GDPR, and the Data Protection Act 2018.
worth_knowing: The Department for Education says almost all schools already restricted phones before the 2026 guidance.

summary: Poland's law banning phones and recording devices in primary schools took effect in September 2026.
school_devices: From September 1, 2026, a July 2026 law bans phones and other communication or recording devices in primary school, with exceptions. It doesn't name smartwatches.
social_media_age: Digital consent age under GDPR is 16. An under-15 limit was proposed in 2026.
child_data_law: GDPR and Poland's Data Protection Act 2018.
worth_knowing: Schools may ask students to hand in devices, with privacy safeguards.

summary: Luxembourg bans phones and connected devices in primary schools and restricts them in secondary schools.
school_devices: Since April 2025, smartphones and connected devices are banned throughout primary school, including breaks. Secondary schools separate phones during lessons.
social_media_age: Digital consent age under GDPR is 16.
child_data_law: GDPR and Luxembourg's 2018 data protection law.
worth_knowing: A national Screen-Life-Balance campaign targets heavy social media use.

summary: France has banned phones in schools by law since 2018 and is expanding phone separation in middle schools.
school_devices: Since 2018, the Education Code bans phones and connected devices in nursery, primary, and middle schools. The 2025 'Portable en pause' program adds storage in middle schools.
social_media_age: Digital consent age under GDPR is 15. A proposed social media age law was still being debated.
child_data_law: GDPR, France's 1978 Data Protection Act, and the 2024 SREN law on age verification.
worth_knowing: Rollout relies on local authorities buying pouches or lockers, so practice varies.

summary: The Netherlands has a national 'no, unless' agreement keeping phones and smartwatches out of classrooms.
school_devices: Since 2024, a national agreement keeps phones and personal devices, including smartwatches, out of class unless needed for learning, health, or safety.
social_media_age: Digital consent age under GDPR is 16.
child_data_law: GDPR and the Dutch implementation act.
worth_knowing: It's a sector agreement, not a law, and a government study found students more social and focused afterward.

summary: Spain's school device rules are set region by region, with no national phone or social media age law.
school_devices: Regional. Madrid's 2025 decree bans personal digital devices in state-funded schools through compulsory secondary; Cantabria requires them off all day.
social_media_age: Digital consent age under GDPR is 14.
child_data_law: GDPR and Organic Law 3/2018.
worth_knowing: Rules differ a lot between regions.

summary: Italy bans smartphones during school hours at every level from the 2025-26 school year.
school_devices: A June 2025 ministry circular extends the smartphone ban to upper secondary schools, following earlier limits for younger grades. It names smartphones, not smartwatches.
social_media_age: Digital consent age under GDPR is 14.
child_data_law: GDPR and the Italian Privacy Code.
worth_knowing: Schools decide how phones are stored and how the ban is enforced.

summary: The US leaves school phone rules to states and has no national social media age limit beyond data rules for under-13s.
school_devices: No federal rule. By 2025-26 many states required districts to restrict phones and personal devices; smartwatch coverage varies. New York's ban is bell to bell.
social_media_age: COPPA requires parental consent to collect data from under-13s. State age laws vary and face court challenges.
child_data_law: Children's Online Privacy Protection Act (COPPA), 1998.
worth_knowing: Kids' watches are sold as walled gardens with parent-approved contacts.

summary: Canada's provinces restrict phones in schools. There is no federal school or social media age rule.
school_devices: Provincial. Ontario, British Columbia, Manitoba, Nova Scotia, Saskatchewan, and others restrict phones, from class-time to all-day limits.
social_media_age: No national rule found.
child_data_law: PIPEDA (2000) plus provincial privacy laws.
worth_knowing: Quebec's 2025 committee recommended an all-day school ban.

summary: Mexico's national school restriction on phones and smart devices starts November 3, 2026, building on rules in 19 states.
school_devices: A September 2026 Education Ministry agreement restricts phones, smart devices, and personal electronics in basic education during the school day from November 3, 2026.
social_media_age: No national rule found.
child_data_law: General Law on Personal Data Protection (2017) and General Law on the Rights of Children and Adolescents (2014).
worth_knowing: Querétaro state proposed banning social media under 14.

summary: Australia bans social media accounts for under-16s nationally. School phone rules are set by states.
school_devices: No national rule. States and territories set school phone bans.
social_media_age: Since December 10, 2025, platforms must stop under-16s from creating or keeping accounts. Platforms, not families, face penalties.
child_data_law: Online Safety Act 2021 (amended 2024) and the Privacy Act 1988.
worth_knowing: Messaging, gaming, and education apps are excluded from the ban. Kids' watches like Spacetalk market themselves as the alternative.

summary: New Zealand's state schools must keep phones away all day, but smartwatches are left to schools.
school_devices: Since 2024, state schools must require phones to be off and away all day, with exceptions. Ministry guidance says smartwatches fall outside the rule.
social_media_age: No rule in force. A 2026 bill would require platforms to block under-16 accounts.
child_data_law: Privacy Act 2020 and the Harmful Digital Communications Act 2015.
worth_knowing: Schools can decide on smartwatches after consulting their communities.

summary: Brazil bans personal electronics in schools, recess included, and passed a dedicated digital statute for children in 2025.
school_devices: Law 15.100/2025 bans students' portable electronics during class, recess, and breaks, with exceptions for learning, health, and accessibility.
social_media_age: The 2025 Digital Statute requires accounts of under-16s to be linked to a guardian, plus age checks for unsuitable services.
child_data_law: Digital Statute of the Child and Adolescent (Law 15.211/2025), with the 1990 child statute and LGPD data law.
worth_knowing: The school law also requires mental health education and staff training on screen use.

summary: Argentina's school rules are regional, and national social media limits are only proposals.
school_devices: No national rule. Buenos Aires City keeps primary students' devices stored and regulates secondary use.
social_media_age: No national rule. Bills propose a ban under 14 or parental consent from 14 to 16.
child_data_law: Law 26.061 (2005) on child protection and Law 25.326 (2000) on personal data.
worth_knowing: Buenos Aires City also requires lessons on responsible social media use.

summary: Chile's 2026 law bans personal mobile devices, including connected smartwatches, in schools.
school_devices: Law 21.801, in force from the 2026 school year, bans personal mobile devices in preschool, primary, and secondary schools, with exceptions.
social_media_age: No national rule found.
child_data_law: Law 21.430 (2022) on children's rights and protection.
worth_knowing: Official guidance names smartwatches with internet or messaging as covered.

summary: Colombia requires schools to set device rules and passed a 2025 law on healthy digital environments for children.
school_devices: Law 2170/2021 requires schools to adopt rules for phone use and allows limits at set times. It is not a national ban.
social_media_age: No national rule. A 2026 bill proposes a minimum age of 14 for social media.
child_data_law: Law 2489/2025 on safe digital environments for children and Law 1581/2012 on personal data.
worth_knowing: The 2025 law directs education and ICT authorities to teach digital citizenship and online safety.
